newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan overnight rate at 0.57%, highest since Sep 95.
newsitem.headline: Japan overnight rate at 0.57%, highest since Sep 95.

text.p: The weighted average of Japan's key overnight call rate surged to 0.57 percent on Monday, the highest rate seen since the Bank of Japan (BOJ) last cut its discount rate on September 8, 1995.
On Friday, the key overnight rate's weighted average was at 0.53 percent.
The rate's rise resulted from disappointment over the BOJ's neutral operation on Monday morning, traders said.

Against expectations of an injection of 200 billion yen or more, the BOJ supplied 100 billion yen to the market on Monday morning, which was just enough to offset a market shortfall of 90 billion yen.
The key overnight rate briefly rose as high as 0.58 percent, although it eased slightly in the afternoon.

When the central bank cut the discount rate, at which it lends to other banks, on September 8, 1995, it also said it would guide the key overnight call rate slightly below the discount rate on average. The discount rate was then halved to the current record low 0.5 percent.
A city bank dealer said the BOJ's operation may have been aimed at finding out whether fund suppliers would buy long-term certificates of deposit (CD) when market rates rise.
A lack of banks' fund-raising by issuing CDs maturing after April 1 was a key factor behind the recent rise in the key overnight rate ahead of the fiscal year-end, traders said.

"Because the BOJ confirmed that investors were not willing to buy the CDs even at higher rates, the bank may conduct an accommodative operation from tomorrow to help ease banks' fund-raising demand before the (fiscal year-end) book closings," the dealer said.
No bids were detected in one-, two- or three-month CDs on Monday. The key three-month CDs were last issued at 0.58 percent on Friday.
